evidence: `GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory.createPair` uses a different CREATE2 salt (including `launchpadLp` and `launchpadFeeDistributor`) when CREATE2ing a pair. The `pairFor()` function (used by `Launchpad` to calculate the pair address) still uses the old salt (just `keccak256(token0, token1)`). This asynchronous behavior causes the pair address calculated by `Launchpad` to differ from the actual pair address created by the Factory, causing transactions referring to the wrong address to fail or assign tokens to an address that does not contain the code (tokens lost).
